direct_answer: Yes. Shell discloses that its “climate change transition plans are delivered through our strategy”, supported by processes and GHG emission reduction targets/ambition, with the aim of becoming “a net-zero emissions energy business by 2050” [Source 1]. Shell states it “supports the more ambitious goal of the Paris Agreement…to 1.5℃” and reports that it believes its net carbon intensity (NCI) targets are aligned with the 1.5℃ goal, describing a methodology derived from IPCC AR6 1.5℃ scenarios (including excluding scenarios overly reliant on removals/bioenergy, removing outliers, and constructing a 1.5℃ pathway) [Source 12]. Shell also states its oil products (Scope 3 Category 11) ambition is compatible with limiting warming to 1.5℃, based on the same IPCC AR6 1.5℃ scenarios and being more ambitious than the median of the scenario range [Source 12]. No timeline for adopting a transition plan is applicable because Shell indicates a transition plan exists and is embedded in its strategy [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: Evidence confirms the existence of a climate mitigation transition plan (embedded in strategy) and provides an explicit explanation of 1.5°C compatibility/alignment for key targets (NCI targets and oil products Scope 3 ambition) with a described methodology based on IPCC AR6 1.5°C scenarios [Source 1, Source 12]. However, the retrieved passages do not provide a complete ESRS E1-1 transition plan description (e.g., full set of actions/levers, detailed implementation roadmap) nor the ESRS E1-4 elements such as whether targets are science-based under a recognised framework, underlying policy/climate scenarios beyond the IPCC AR6 reference, and whether targets have been externally assured.
disclosure_gaps: Clear statement that the transition plan as a whole (not only specific targets) is aligned with limiting warming to 1.5°C, including how all material emissions (Scopes 1, 2, and relevant Scope 3 categories) are addressed in the plan (only partial target alignment evidence is provided) [Source 12].

ESRS E1-4 details on whether GHG targets are “science-based” under a recognised framework/methodology (e.g., SBTi) and related disclosures (only an internal methodology based on IPCC AR6 scenarios is described for NCI and oil products ambition) [Source 12].

Disclosure of underlying climate and policy scenarios used for targets beyond the general reference to IPCC AR6 1.5°C scenarios (no specific scenario names/parameters provided in retrieved text) [Source 12].
Whether the targets/transition plan have been externally assured (no assurance information in retrieved passages).
If applicable under ESRS E1-1.16, more detail on decarbonisation levers/actions and how they map to targets (the passages reference that such levers exist but do not include them) [Source 1].
key_findings: Shell states it has a climate change mitigation transition plan delivered through its strategy, supported by processes and GHG reduction targets/ambition, aiming for net-zero by 2050 [Source 1].

Shell states it supports the Paris Agreement 1.5°C goal and believes its NCI targets are aligned with 1.5°C, using a pathway derived from IPCC AR6 1.5°C scenarios with specified filtering/processing steps [Source 12].

Shell states its oil products Scope 3 Category 11 ambition (15–20% reduction by 2030 vs 2021) is compatible with 1.5°C based on IPCC AR6 1.5°C scenarios and being more ambitious than the median of the scenario range [Source 12].
